items: Medical Investigation: Request a T4 thyroid panel test to check for hyperthyroidism, which commonly causes increased vocalization as an early symptom before weight loss or other obvious signs appear.

Medical Investigation: Request an SDMA blood test to detect early-stage kidney disease, as cats with chronic kidney disease frequently vocalize more—especially during nighttime hours when they're restless.

Medical Investigation: Ask your vet to assess your cat for chronic pain conditions like arthritis, which cats instinctively hide and often express through increased vocalization when moving or being handled.

Medical Investigation: Seek a veterinary behaviorist referral if all medical tests return normal but excessive vocalization persists beyond one year, as prescription medication can support long-term behavior retraining.

Track Meowing Patterns: Record each meowing episode for at least 7 consecutive days, noting time of day, location, what you were doing beforehand, your cat's behavior before meowing started, and your response.

Track Meowing Patterns: Document how long each meowing episode lasts and what eventually stops it, which reveals whether the behavior self-terminates or continues until you respond with attention or action.

Track Meowing Patterns: Identify which of four vocalization patterns your cat exhibits—pre-feeding, post-isolation, demand-driven, or ambient anxiety—because each pattern requires a different retraining approach.

Track Meowing Patterns: Stop all interventions until the 7-day log is complete, because random attempts to fix the behavior can accidentally reinforce it and make the problem worse before you understand it.

Retrain the Behavior: Implement total extinction by removing every response to meowing, including verbal scolding, eye contact, physical comfort, and even sighing, because any response trains the cat to keep meowing.

Retrain the Behavior: Introduce an alternative quiet behavior and reward it with treats, play, or affection immediately, so your cat learns that silence produces better results than persistent vocalization.
Retrain the Behavior: Feed meals at consistent, predictable times every day to eliminate food-demand meowing, because irregular feeding schedules teach cats that meowing gets food attention.

Retrain the Behavior: Reduce household stress using pheromone diffusers, consistent daily routines, and night lights for senior cats, because ambient anxiety contributes significantly to ongoing vocalization.
